# Saṅkhārupapatti Sutta (MN 120 (PTS MN iii 99))

**ID:** MN 120 (PTS MN iii 99)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Saṅkhārupapatti Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** Rebirth by Choice
**PTS:** MN iii 99
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅkhārupapatti Sutta* ("Rebirth by Choice" or "Reappearance by Aspiration") is the 120th discourse of the Majjhimanikāya, delivered by the Buddha at Jeta's Grove in Sāvatthi [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. The text sets out how a practitioner can consciously determine their future rebirth through intentional aspiration and resolve [Devdas 2004; Fronsdal 1998]. A monk endowed with five spiritual qualities—faith (*saddhā*), virtue (*sīla*), learning (*suta*), generosity (*cāga*), and wisdom (*paññā*)—can formulate a wish to be reborn in a prosperous human birth or in various celestial realms; by fixing and cultivating the mind upon that resolve, he reappears accordingly after death [Allon, Senior Manuscripts; Anālayo 2010; Fronsdal 1998; Lim Hwee San 2009]. The discourse maps out an extensive Buddhist cosmology, surveying the various heavenly realms including the subdivisions of the Brahmā worlds (such as the *ābhā* and *subhā* devas) and formless spheres [Anālayo 2018; Buddhaghosa & Ñāṇamoli 2010; Nattier, Names of Amitābha]. However, it concludes by emphasizing that one may direct this aspiration beyond the realms of the gods toward the destruction of the taints (*āsavakkhaya*), attaining arahantship and *nibbāna* here and now [Allon, Senior Manuscripts; Rogell 2003].

Curated parallels include a full parallel in the Chinese *Madhyamāgama* (MĀ 168, *Yìxíng jīng* 意行經) and partial parallels in the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (AN 4.123–124) [Stuart 2012]. A fragmentary Gāndhārī witness preserving parts of this sutra has also been identified in scroll RS 10 of the Senior Manuscripts collection [Allon, Senior Manuscripts]. In agreement with curated records, DharmaNexus aligns the sutta with the Chinese *Madhyamāgama* (T 26) as well as the Tibetan *Karmavibhaṅga* (D0338) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects extensive Pali-internal text reuse with cosmological lists in the *Aṭṭhakanipāta* (AN 8), the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), and various Saṁyuttas concerning specific classes of rebirth, including the *Gandhabbakāya* (SN 31), *Nāga* (SN 29), *Supaṇṇa* (SN 30), and *Valāhaka* (SN 32) Saṁyuttas [DharmaNexus].
